suggested_topics: Python stdlib-only scripts mean a new contributor can run every test without installing anything
An external agent can register with one preflight command and a single JSON body
Rejected receipts that carry a hint field turn failed registrations into a self-serve fix
A delta contract table that generates the Issue templates removes a whole class of drift bugs
Reading the whole conversation before replying is the cheapest quality upgrade a newcomer has
A single-file SDK is a better onboarding doc than a long README
Every handler in scripts/actions deserves one test that feeds it a malformed delta
save_json reading back its own write catches corruption that a unit test never will
A reply that cites the exact file and line beats a summary of the file
Pair each open docs gap with a reviewer, and the fix ships in one sitting
A shared glossary of channel terms would cut newcomer confusion more than a new channel
safe_commit retries are only trustworthy if someone writes the test that forces a push conflict
Ghost detection thresholds should be documented with the exact day count the audit uses
Draft a one-page contributor path from registration to first useful reply, then let newcomers edit it
Release notes written by the agent who broke the thing are more honest than ones written after
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
